blocks.text: 12 Best n8n Alternatives in 2026

The 12 best n8n alternatives in 2026, with prices and licenses checked on each vendor site: Zapier, Make, Activepieces, Pipedream, Windmill, Node-RED, Temporal, Kestra and more, plus a guide to picking one when you leave n8n.

The best n8n alternatives in 2026 are Make (managed, no infrastructure to run, 3,000+ apps), Zapier (easiest to learn, 9,000+ apps), and Activepieces (self-hostable, with an MIT-licensed community edition). If you moved to n8n from Zapier for cost reasons and find the self-hosting overhead too high, Make hits a solid middle ground. If you want to keep self-hosting, look at Windmill, Node-RED and Kestra.

n8n's learning curve is real. Teams without a developer on staff often spend more time managing the infrastructure than the automation saves. That trade-off is what most comparisons skip. n8n is also fair-code, not open source: its Sustainable Use License limits use to your own internal business, non-commercial or personal purposes, which matters if you plan to resell or host workflows for clients.

This guide compares 12 n8n alternatives with feature depth, pricing as published on each vendor's own pricing page (checked September 26, 2026), and a framework for picking the right workflow platform for how your team actually ships. We did not run hands-on tests for this list; every fact comes from the vendor's site, docs or GitHub repo.
Best n8n alternatives: a brief overview
Zapier: Best for non-technical teams that need 9,000+ app integrations and zero hosting overhead.
Make: Best for visual builders who want power-user features without writing code.
Activepieces: Best for teams that love n8n's ethos but want a cleaner UX and AI-first design.
Pipedream: Best for developers who want serverless workflows with real code (Node.js, Python, Go, Bash).
Windmill: Best for developers who want to keep self-hosting but write scripts instead of wiring nodes.
Node-RED: Best for event-driven and IoT flows on your own hardware, under an Apache 2.0 license.
Workato: Best for enterprise IT teams that need governance, SSO, and recipe libraries.
Tray.ai: Best for revenue and customer ops teams running mission-critical SaaS integrations.
Latenode: Best for builders who want low-code plus AI nodes and headless browser automation.
Inngest: Best for engineering teams building event-driven, durable workflows in their own code.
Temporal: Best for engineering teams that need true durable execution at any scale.
Kestra: Best for data and platform teams that want workflows as YAML, versioned like code.
If you are leaving n8n but want to keep running the engine yourself, GitHub stars are one rough signal of how big each self-hostable project's community is. n8n itself is shown for scale.
GitHub stars of self-hostable n8n alternatives
Source: GitHub repository pages (n8n-io/n8n, kestra-io/kestra, activepieces/activepieces, node-red/node-red, temporalio/temporal, windmill-labs/windmill, inngest/inngest), checked 2026-09-26.
1. Zapier, best for non-technical teams and breadth of integrations

Zapier is the platform most people compare n8n against first, and for good reason. It lists 9,000+ connected apps on its pricing page, about four times the 2,274 integrations n8n lists, and it is the path of least resistance for marketing, sales, ops, and finance teams who do not want to think about hosting, error queues, or YAML.

Where n8n rewards engineers, Zapier rewards operators. Workflows ("Zaps") are linear and obvious; the editor hides complexity; and the Tables, Interfaces, and Agents products extend Zapier into a small operational platform without forcing a separate tool.
Key features
9,000+ app integrations, including SaaS tools n8n does not natively support
AI-powered Zap creation and natural-language step authoring
Tables, Interfaces, and Agents extend beyond pure workflow automation
Multi-step paths, filters, and formatter steps without code
SOC 2 Type II audited; Zapier's Terms of Service forbid uploading protected health information regulated by HIPAA
Best for
Marketing and sales ops teams without engineering capacity
Solo founders and small businesses connecting many SaaS tools
Teams that value time-to-first-working-Zap over per-task cost
Pricing
Free plan with 100 tasks/mo
Professional from $19.99/mo billed annually ($29.99 month to month), Team from $69/mo billed annually; Enterprise is custom
Pros
9,000+ app integrations, about four times n8n's listed count
Fast non-technical onboarding: linear Zaps with no hosting to set up
Stable infra with well-understood error semantics
Cons
Per-task pricing becomes expensive at high volume compared to self-hosted n8n
Less control over branching, loops, and complex data transforms than n8n or Make
Not an option for protected health information: Zapier's Terms of Service prohibit sending it
Free weekly brief
Steal our production automations
The exact n8n flows, Claude Code setups, and prompts we ship for clients, broken down step by step. No spam, unsubscribe anytime.
2. Make, best for visual builders who want depth without code

Make (formerly Integromat) sits between Zapier and n8n. Like Zapier it is fully SaaS with no hosting, but its canvas-style editor and operator model feel closer to n8n's node graph. Make suits power users who want to manipulate JSON, route arrays, and build conditional logic without dropping into a code editor.

If you outgrew Zapier because you needed iterators, aggregators, and complex routers, Make is usually the next stop. Compared to n8n, Make trades self-hosting and code nodes for a more polished visual experience and a managed infra you do not have to babysit. If you are weighing the move the other way, our Make alternatives guide covers it from Make's side.
Key features
Visual scenario builder with iterators, aggregators, and routers
3,000+ apps with deep API coverage for major apps
Credit-based pricing: each module action counts as one credit
AI-assisted scenario creation and module suggestions
Make Grid, an auto-generated map of your scenarios and AI automations
Best for
Marketing, ecommerce, and ops teams that need branching logic
Agencies running automations across many client workspaces
Visual thinkers who want power without writing JavaScript
Pricing
Free plan with 1,000 credits/mo and 2 active scenarios
Core from $9/mo, Pro from $16/mo, Teams from $29/mo (10,000 credits each); Enterprise is custom
Pros
Visual routing and data shaping without writing code
Strong cost efficiency at moderate volume
Granular control over per-module retries and error handling
Cons
No self-hosting option (Enterprise adds only an on-prem agent for reaching local systems), which rules it out for some compliance regimes
Steeper learning curve than Zapier for first-time users
3. Activepieces, best for n8n loyalists who want a cleaner UX

Activepieces is the closest spiritual successor to n8n among the new generation of workflow tools. Its community edition is MIT-licensed (enterprise directories carry a separate commercial license), self-hostable, and built around a piece-based architecture similar to nodes. The big differentiator is design: Activepieces feels modern out of the box, with AI features built into the editor rather than bolted on.

For teams that love the n8n philosophy (own your runtime, control your data, write code when you need to) but find n8n's UI dated, Activepieces is worth a serious look. Its GitHub repo had 24,738 stars on September 26, 2026.
Key features
MIT-licensed community edition with self-host (Docker, Kubernetes, air-gapped) and managed cloud options
AI agents, plain-language flow building, and an MCP server so Claude and Cursor can run your flows
760+ pieces, each MIT-licensed
Branches, loops, and HTTP/code pieces for custom logic
Per-flow versioning and history
Best for
Teams that want n8n's ownership model with a modern editor
Builders integrating AI workflows alongside traditional automation
Agencies offering self-hosted automation to clients
Pricing
Free self-hosted community edition; free cloud plan with 100 credits a day
Plus $20/mo flat (10,000 credits, up to 5 users), Team $200/mo flat; Ultimate is custom
Pros
Clean, modern editor compared to n8n
AI-native design reduces time-to-build for LLM workflows
MIT license avoids the restrictions of n8n's Sustainable Use License
Cons
Smaller integration catalog than n8n or Zapier (760+ pieces vs n8n's 2,274 listed integrations)
Younger ecosystem means fewer community templates and tutorials
4. Pipedream, best for developers who want serverless workflows with real code

Pipedream is what you build if you believe workflows should be code, not nodes. Each step in a Pipedream workflow can run Node.js, Python, Go or Bash, and the platform handles triggers, scheduling, state, and observability. There is still a visual layer, but the substance is code, which makes it a natural choice for engineering teams that find drag-and-drop tools limiting.

Compared to n8n, Pipedream is more developer-pure. You write the logic; the platform runs it. There is no hosting to manage, but you also do not own the runtime the way you would with self-hosted n8n. Workday signed an agreement to acquire Pipedream on November 19, 2025; the public Free to Business plans were still listed on Pipedream's pricing page on September 26, 2026.
Key features
Code steps in Node.js, Python, Go, or Bash with npm and PyPI package access
3,000+ integrated apps as a starting point for custom logic
Real-time event inspector with full payloads and logs
Built-in data stores, file stores, and secret management
Bi-directional GitHub Sync on paid plans
Best for
Backend and platform engineers automating internal processes
Teams building data pipelines and webhook-based integrations
Engineers who dislike visual editors but want zero infra
Pricing
Free plan with a daily credit limit and a limited number of active workflows (one credit is 30 seconds of compute at 256 MB)
Basic $29/mo and Advanced $49/mo billed annually; Connect $99/mo; Business is custom with SSO, HIPAA support and SLAs
Pros
True code, true package ecosystem, true debuggability
Free tier for prototyping
Easy to graduate from a quick script to a production workflow
Cons
Non-developers will struggle; this is not a tool for ops users
Self-hosting is not an option; the runtime is fully managed
5. Windmill, best for self-hosted, code-first workflows and internal tools

Windmill is the pick for developers who left n8n because they spent more time fighting nodes than writing logic. You write scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Bash or SQL, and Windmill turns each one into a webhook, a schedulable job and an auto-generated UI. Scripts chain into flows, which Windmill models as DAGs, and a low-code app editor builds internal tools on top.

Like n8n, you can self-host it with Docker or Kubernetes, so your data stays on your infrastructure. The license needs a careful read: the core is AGPLv3, but the Community Edition images also contain proprietary code you may use free, within set limits, and not resell or offer as a managed service.
Key features
Scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Bash and SQL, each with an autogenerated webhook
Flows as DAGs with schedules and triggers
Auto-generated UIs for every script and flow, plus a drag-and-drop app editor
Self-host with Docker or Kubernetes, or use Windmill Cloud
Audit logs, SAML and 24/7 priority support on Enterprise
Best for
Engineering teams replacing n8n Code nodes with real scripts under version control
Ops and data teams that need internal tools and workflows in one place
Companies that must self-host but have no appetite for n8n's license terms
Pricing
Free cloud plan (up to 10 users, unlimited executions, community support); free self-hosted Community Edition
Enterprise from $120/mo on cloud, with developer seats at $20/mo and operator seats at $10/mo; workers billed at $50 per worker per month
Pros
Code is the primary interface, so logic lives in reviewable scripts rather than node configs
One tool covers scripts, workflows and internal UIs
Self-hosted in the same way teams already run n8n
Cons
The self-hosted Community Edition caps you at 3 workspaces, 50 users and 4 groups, with no agent workers
Mixed licensing (AGPLv3 core plus proprietary code in the Community Edition images) needs a legal read before you build a product on it
Skip it if your automation builders do not write code. Windmill's strength is scripts, and a no-code team will get more from Make or Activepieces.
6. Node-RED, best for event-driven and IoT flows on your own hardware

Node-RED is the tool on this list whose editor looks most like n8n: a browser-based canvas where you wire nodes into flows. It started in 2013 at IBM's Emerging Technology Services group and is now an OpenJS Foundation project under the Apache 2.0 license, so there is no commercial license to negotiate and no vendor to lose.

Its runtime is built on Node.js and is light enough to run on a Raspberry Pi, which is why it is common in industrial, home automation and edge projects. Flows are stored as JSON you can export and share. For teams leaving n8n over license terms and mostly handling device, MQTT or event data, it is a strong fit.
Key features
Browser-based flow editor with a palette of nodes
Flows stored as JSON for import, export and sharing
Community flow library with over 5,000 nodes and flows
Runs locally, in Docker, on devices like Raspberry Pi, or in the cloud
Apache 2.0 license, governed by the OpenJS Foundation
Best for
IoT, industrial and edge teams processing device and sensor data
Developers who want a free, permissively licensed visual flow tool
Teams that need automation to run on-site on low-cost hardware
Pricing
Free and open source (Apache 2.0); you pay only for the machine you run it on
Managed hosting comes from third parties such as FlowFuse, AWS and Azure, not from the Node-RED project
Pros
Permissive license with no usage restrictions of the kind n8n's Sustainable Use License sets
Lightweight enough for edge devices
Large community library of nodes and flows
Cons
Most integrations come from the community library, so check each node's maintenance before you depend on it
No first-party managed cloud; you run and secure it yourself or pick a third-party host
Skip it if your workflows are mostly SaaS-to-SaaS business automation. Zapier, Make or Activepieces ship far more ready-made business app connectors.
7. Workato, best for enterprise IT and governance

Workato is the enterprise iPaaS that competes with MuleSoft and Boomi more than it does with n8n. Where n8n is bottom-up and developer-led, Workato is top-down and IT-led. It ships with role-based access control, recipe libraries, environment management, compliance controls, and a partner ecosystem geared toward large IT departments.
If your buying motion involves a CIO, a security review, and a procurement cycle, Workato is built for that conversation in a way n8n is not.
Key features
Centralized governance: identity, policy, approvals, observability and cost controls across agents, workflows and APIs
Multi-agent building, deployment and operation alongside classic recipes
API Gateway and API Management for exposing workflows as managed APIs
Connects to 17,000+ apps, APIs, databases, files and MCP servers, per Workato's homepage
Embedded iPaaS for ISVs to ship integrations inside their product
Best for
Mid-market and enterprise IT and integration teams
Companies needing strict SOX, HIPAA, or SOC 2 controls
